title: Pizza Tower: Peppino's elastic expression shapes

people.name: Pizza Tower Guy (McPig)
people.role: Programming and animations, self-described in the 2019 developer interview

summary: A useful upper limit for expression amplitude: the face changes silhouette as well as internal eye and mouth shapes.

observations.text: The three-pose Peppino illustration contrasts a huge horizontal tooth-and-mouth opening with a tiny puckered mouth. The eyes protrude beyond the head mass and shift together toward the object of attention.

The creator says his drawing approach lets him animate quickly without keeping identical proportions in every drawing. This supports controlled proportion changes, but does not establish a particular frame count or timing curve.

mistIdeas: Our inference: make a surprised MIST pose change the spacing and height of both eyes before adding extra effects. Let the silhouette carry the reaction.
Our inference: reserve a short eye-shape overshoot for exceptional surprise, then recover to MIST's normal proportions. Preserve its own face design and palette.
Our inference: test a tiny compressed mouth against a much wider peak mouth. These distinct key poses may read better than several subtly different smiles.

media.credit: Pizza Tower Guy / Tour De Pizza; published with creator interview by Gaming Reinvented

title: ANTONBLAST: Anton's open-mouth to clenched-teeth reaction

people.name: Juniper / PinPan
people.role: Lead gameplay animator on AntonBlast, self-credited on artist profile

summary: An official eight-second close-up shows how mouth area and silhouette can dominate a reaction without requiring detailed facial anatomy.

observations.text: At the inspected start of the official clip, Anton has a tall open mouth, separated upper and lower tooth bands and raised arms. At the inspected end, the mouth becomes a large clenched white tooth mass, with narrow eyes and a raised fist. These are sharply different readable shapes.
The dark hair and beard create an angular outline around the bright mouth. The face is not limited to moving small features inside an unchanged oval.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give surprise and determined recovery genuinely different mouth silhouettes instead of scaling one mouth path.
Our inference: test a compressed anticipatory eye pose, a single large reaction peak, and a smaller settled expression. This proposed sequence is a MIST experiment, not measured ANTONBLAST timing.
Our inference: keep MIST's outer housing stable while allowing its digital eye and mouth graphics to deform strongly inside it. Copy the contrast of shapes, not Anton's teeth, beard or colour scheme.

title: BattleBlock Theater: simple faces with authored puppet movement

people.name: Derek Lieu
people.role: Cutscene animator for the nine shipped game cutscenes

people.name: Dan Paladin
people.role: Art, storyboards and rough opening animatic; art and animation for the 2011 opening/prologue

summary: The closest structural lesson for MIST: an extremely simple face can act through the movement of the whole graphic and carefully chosen reaction shapes.

observations.text: The official finished cutscene still uses tiny eyes and large open mouths on white, flat characters. Round, square and irregular heads remain readable against a busy purple scene.

Lieu describes sketching puppet motion paths, manually keyframing rotation and offsetting Hatty from the boat movement to avoid rigid attachment. He also describes adjustable inertial overshoot and settling.
The production began with Paladin's rough drawings and story beats, which Lieu animated before swapping in final artwork. This is evidence for testing acting before surface polish.

mistIdeas: Our inference: validate MIST reactions as rough eye-and-mouth poses before adding glow, noise or shading.
Our inference: offset eye arrival, mouth arrival and whole-face settle slightly so a reaction does not resemble one rigid layer being scaled.
Our inference: try a small rotation or translation overshoot followed by a deliberate readable hold. Tune recovery to the event's importance; avoid making every idle movement bounce.
Our inference: preserve simple facial marks and spend the motion budget on clear staging, gaze direction and purposeful pauses.
